A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
childhood focal epilepsie syndromes are a heterogeneous group of diseases, but with a common pathophysiological mechanism.
SRPX2 and/or ELP4 mutations may be involved in the development of rolandic epilepsy and in some cases of LKS/CSWS, and may contribute to the cognitive deficits associated with these disorders.

the genetic factors that contribute to the development and maintenance of these syndromes are not only the genes responsible for the epileptogenic focus but also the genes that are involved in the regulation of the developmental processes of the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the study of these rare epileptic syndroms may provide important information on the mechanisms involved in the development and maturation of the brain and on the genetic bases of focal epilepsies in childhood.
childhood focal epilepsias, including LKS, CSWS, and rolandic epilepsy (RE), are genetically heterogeneous diseases with a complex mode of inheritance, involving several genes and loci.
